# Fixed-point component and concealment vectors

These fixtures are generated by the scalar C implementation at revision
`503d81b138d76621aae4b12786e90de48aa8db3a`. The generators link the independently
built fixed-point reference; they never obtain expected values from Rust.
Tests consume committed files and require no C compiler or FFI.

Build the reference first with `tools/reference/build.sh fixed`.

| Generator under `tools/reference/` | Covered results |
| --- | --- |
| `extract_fixed_mdct_table.py` | Canonical static Q15 MDCT twiddles |
| `generate_fixed_transform_vectors.py` | 16 FFT and 32 MDCT forward/backward cases, including overlap state and strides |
| `generate_fixed_vq_vectors.py` | Current Q24 normalization, rotation, search, quantization, entropy packets, and band scaling |
| `generate_fixed_tone_vectors.py` | 201 normalization, LPC, tone-detection, and acos operations, including 1,160 acos arguments |
| `generate_fixed_math_vectors.py` | 9,108 square-root, reciprocal, cosine, arctangent, and division results |
| `generate_fixed_plc_vectors.py` | Periodic concealment LPC/history/PCM hashes, energy ratios, and four five-frame packet-loss streams |

Run each Python generator from any directory. The PLC packet fixtures cover
8 kHz and 24 kHz mono, 24 kHz stereo, and 48 kHz high-amplitude noise. They check
every decoded integer sample and float bit pattern, as well as final entropy
ranges. The inherited PLC priming packet bytes are preserved in
`fixed-plc-prime.script`; current C produces their state hashes.

The `fixed-vq.script` rotation cases with length equal to stride preserve the
required Q24-to-Q14 rounding even when the butterfly has no sample pairs.

The PLC generator accepts `--res24`, `--qext` and `--pfa` independently.
Build the corresponding reference profile first, for example
`sh tools/reference/build.sh fixed-res24-qext-pfa`, then run
`python3 tools/reference/generate_fixed_plc_vectors.py --res24 --qext --pfa`.
Eight fixture sets preserve each profile's exact PCM conversion, transform
rounding and decoder state. The tests select the matching set rather than
applying 16-bit PCM expectations to a 24-bit decoder.
